entries.name: Curated Libraries
entries.description: Forked and updated from the above list.

entries.name: Portacle
entries.description: A portable and multiplatform Common Lisp environment. It ships a slightly customized Emacs with SLIME, SBCL (a popular Common Lisp implementation), Quicklisp and Git. No installation needed, so it's a very quick and easy way to get going.

entries.name: Lispbox
entries.description: An IDE (Emacs + SLIME), Common Lisp implementation (Clozure Common Lisp) and library manager (Quicklisp), pre-packaged as archives for Windows, macOS and Linux. Descendant of "Lisp in a Box" mentioned in Practical Common Lisp.

entries.name: Lispworks Personal Edition
entries.description: A non-Emacs based IDE for LispWorks Lisp, with some restrictions.

entries.name: Allegro Common Lisp
entries.description: Has a free Express Edition IDE, and training videos on YouTube.

entries.name: Articulate Common Lisp
entries.description: A HOWTO for putting together a Lisp environment, and has information on useful libraries and how to structure projects.

entries.name: Emacs
entries.description: user, you can just install SLIME and a supported Common Lisp implementation. See the SLIME manual for more details.

entries.name: installing an implementation
entries.description: using an implementation manager like Roswell, or on Docker.

entries.name: Chapter 7
entries.description: Covers the Common Lisp Object System (CLOS).

entries.name: The ANSI Common Lisp Standard Draft
entries.description: The last draft version of the ANSI INCITS 226-1994 (previously ANSI X3.226-1994) standard.

entries.name: The Common Lisp Cookbook
entries.description: A list of useful Lisp recipes. Also contains a list of other online sources of CL information.

entries.name: Cliki on CLtL2
entries.description: Claims it has more useful descriptions of LOOP and FORMAT than the CLHS does.

entries.name: Stack Overflow on CLtL2
entries.description: Some recommend using CLtL2 for insight and inspiration, but to use the CLHS when programming.

entries.name: A list of differences between CLtL2 and the ANSI Common Lisp specification.
Chapter 28
entries.description: Covers the Common Lisp Object System.

entries.name: Common Lisp the Language (2nd Edition) by Guy L. Steele
entries.description: A description of the Common Lisp language from just before it was standardized by ANSI. Don't use it as a reference.

entries.name: Common Lisp: A Gentle Introduction to Symbolic Computation by David S. Touretzky
entries.description: a good introduction for people new to programming. Contains code for really useful utilities like DTRACE and SDRAW.

entries.name: Common Lisp: An interactive approach by Stuart C. Shapiro
entries.description: A textbook that teaches mainly through the use of exercises.

entries.name: Practical Common Lisp by Peter Seibel
entries.description: A great introduction for experienced programmers, and tries to highlight from the very beginning what makes CL different to other languages.

entries.name: Common Lisp Koans
entries.description: Not exactly a book, but a set of koans to help you learn the language.

entries.name: On Lisp by Paul Graham
entries.description: A great book for intermediately experienced Lispers.

entries.name: Comments on Let Over Lambda
entries.description: Several people recommend that you be comfortable with On Lisp before reading this book, and that the start is slow.

entries.name: The chapter on closures
entries.description: Has several non-trivial examples, and demonstrates the power of this feature.

entries.name: Let Over Lambda by Doug Hoyte
entries.description: An advanced book on Lisp Macros.

entries.name: Paradigms of Artificial Intelligence Programming by Peter Norvig
entries.description: Has many interesting applications of Lisp, but is no longer a good reference for AI.

entries.name: Land of Lisp by Conrad Barski, MD
entries.description: A fun introduction to Lisp that uses comics and has you writing games.

entries.name: Chapter 1
entries.description: and Chapter 2 are available online.

entries.name: ANSI Common Lisp by Paul Graham
entries.description: Good as a reference, covers CLOS, and has several example program implementations.

entries.name: Common Lisp Recipes by Edmund Weitz
entries.description: A great set of Common Lisp patterns.

entries.name: Object-Oriented Programming in Common Lisp by Sonya E. Keene
entries.description: An in-depth description of the CLOS, and shows how to use it with example applications.

entries.name: modern public domain CLOS MOP specification
entries.description: by Jean-Philippe Paradis (Hexstream).

entries.name: Chapters 5 and 6 (available online)
entries.description: The specification of a metaobject protocol extension to CLOS, by Robert Strandh.

entries.name: Adam Tornhill on AMOP
entries.description: Recommends reading Practical Common Lisp, then Object-Oriented Programming in Common Lisp, and then AMOP.

entries.name: The Art of the Metaobject Protocol by Gregor Kiczales, Jim des Rivieres, and Daniel G. Bobrow
entries.description: Describes the CLOS Metaobject Protocol (MOP).

entries.name: Cliki
entries.description: The Common Lisp Wiki. A great resource for all things CL. Has a great Getting Started page and an extensive list of Lisp books.

entries.name: other rooms
entries.description: on the Libera.Chat network are great places for learning about Common Lisp. (Freenode should be avoided.)

entries.name: Common Lisp Subreddit
entries.description: The Subreddit for Common Lisp.

entries.name: Lisp Subreddit
entries.description: An active community, and has loads of useful links and reference documents in the sidebar.

entries.name: Lisp Discord server
entries.description: Is a Discord for Lisp. Has a channel dedicated to Common Lisp and will happily answer questions.

entries.name: Quickdocs
entries.description: Documentation for projects in Quicklisp.

entries.name: State of the Common Lisp Ecosystem, 2015
entries.description: Article about what libraries you should use, and why.

entries.name: Articulate Common Lisp
entries.description: Lists some useful libraries.

entries.name: CMUCL manual and other useful information
LispWorks
entries.description: Commercial, but as mentioned previously, has a Personal Edition with minor limitations.

entries.name: Steel Bank Common Lisp (SBCL)
entries.description: My personal favorite.

entries.name: Scieneer Common Lisp (SCL)
entries.description: A commercial Linux and Unix implementation, but has an unrestricted free evaluation and non-commercial use version.
